summary: Gibbet Hill lookout in Groton: wooden tower from 1941, 68-foot steel tower built 1957; a 2026 trail write-up says it is still staffed in fire season (one secondhand account).

facts.design: 68-foot steel tower with 10x10 wooden cab and a smaller cab below
facts.status_note: The official record is the 2004 register entry; a 2026 visitor account says the tower is still staffed in fire season. No official record since 2004.

resolved_conflicts.field: name of the stone ruin on Gibbet Hill
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Trailspotting titles its page 'Bancroft's Castle, Groton Fire Tower, MA', but its text describes the stone bungalow ruin that burned in 1932 and, separately, the 68-foot steel Groton Fire Tower that it says is still staffed in fire season. The Groton Trails page describes the ruin only. The title runs the two together; the text does not.

notes_for_editor: The 2004 register is the only official source. Trailspotting (Aug 2026) describes the steel tower as still staffed during fire season and says visitors were invited up by the operator; this is one secondhand account, so confidence stays low and public access is not established. Groton Trails describes the stone ruin only. Ffla.org and firelookout.org state-tower pages returned 404, so the state tower number and operation date in search snippets are unverified and not used. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the story's 'no later source' sentence was contradicted by the Trailspotting page and was rewritten; the 1940 Lowell Sun item was missing from events and has been added.
